heads.text: MASS EXODUS: BRING YOUR OWN SOCKS
THOUSANDS FLEE; FEW REMEMBER THE KETTLE
ARMY ARRIVES TO FIND NOBODY HOME
REFUGEES ON ROAD, POT ROAST LEFT IN OVEN

bodies.text: Refugees of {entity2} have fled {site} ahead of an advancing {entity_race} army of {entity}, led by {hf}, {source} reports. Witnesses say the evacuation was swift, orderly, and left behind at least one perfectly good barrel of ale, which experts call the real tragedy.

According to {source}, the {entity2_race} residents of {site} packed up and left {ago} as {entity} marched in under {hf}. Local officials described the departure as 'strategic,' 'temporary' and 'very, very fast.'

News reached {fort} via {source}: {site} has been abandoned by its people, who fled the approaching forces of {entity}. The army's commander, {hf}, reportedly arrived to find only a cat, who refused to surrender.

Refugees streamed out of {site} {ago} ahead of {hf} and the {entity_race} host of {entity}, says {source}. The fortress bookkeeper asks that any refugees reaching {fort} bring their own beds, mugs and, ideally, a useful skill other than running.

Word from {source} confirms that {entity2} has fled {site} rather than face the army of {entity}. Military analysts praise the decision, noting that running away has a perfect record against being stabbed.
An army of {entity}, led by {hf}, has sent the population of {site} scattering into the hills, according to {source}. The refugees are said to be cold, hungry and, worst of all, entirely without ale.

The {entity2_race} folk of {site} have taken to the roads, {source} tells us, fleeing {entity} and its commander {hf}. Our manager notes that refugees are welcome at {fort} provided they do not bring the army along with them.

Word from {source}: {site} is emptying fast as {entity} advances. Fleeing residents reportedly left in such a hurry that several are still wearing only one sock, a fashion our correspondent calls 'brave.'
{hf} and the forces of {entity} drove the residents of {site} into flight {ago}, reports {source}. Asked for comment, one refugee said only, 'Is that a goblin?' and resumed running.
Refugees fleeing {site} report that {entity} is coming, and coming hard, says {source}. The {entity_race} army found the town deserted and is said to be quite annoyed, having prepared a speech.

heads.text: OCCUPIERS MOVE IN, COMPLAIN ABOUT DECOR
TOWN CHANGES HANDS, KEEPS SAME MUD
OCCUPATION BEGINS; NOBODY ASKED THE CAT
LANDLORDS BY FORCE: A TRADITION CONTINUES

bodies.text: {entity}, a {entity_race} power, has occupied {site} and evicted {entity2}, {source} reports. The new occupants are said to be settling in, rearranging the furniture and already arguing over who gets the room with the window.
According to {source}, {site} is now under the control of {entity} following the eviction of the {entity2_race} government of {entity2}. Rents are expected to rise. Rents are always expected to rise.

The {entity_race} forces of {entity} occupied {site} {ago}, says {source}. {entity2} was evicted without notice, without deposit and, witnesses say, without their good boots, which are now being worn by somebody else entirely.

{site} has a new landlord. {source} tells us {entity} marched in and showed {entity2} the door. Our legal correspondent notes that conquest is not a recognised grounds for eviction, but is extremely effective.
Reports from {source} confirm {entity} now holds {site}, with {hf} reportedly in charge. The evicted {entity2} have filed a complaint with the relevant authority, which is also {entity}.

Occupation news via {source}: the {entity_race} banner of {entity} now flies over {site}. The evicted {entity2_race} population is said to be furious, homeless and, in the words of one, 'not even allowed to take the good chairs.'
{entity} has taken {site} from {entity2}, according to {source}. Occupying troops have reportedly posted new rules on every door, including a ban on complaining and a curfew on the word 'liberation.'
The town of {site} changed hands {ago}, {source} reports, as {entity} evicted {entity2} and moved in. Locals say the main difference so far is that the new owners leave far more bones in the well.

Word reaching {fort} from {source}: {site} is under {entity_race} occupation. {entity} reportedly evicted the previous residents, then spent three days looking for where they hid the ale. They did not find it. Good.
Word via {source} is that {entity} has occupied {site} under the leadership of {hf}. The evicted {entity2} are said to be regrouping, sulking, and composing a strongly worded song.

heads.text: ARMY KNOCKS; DOES NOT WAIT FOR ANSWER
SIEGE AT {site}: SWORDS OUT, MANNERS IN

bodies.text: {entity} has attacked {site}, {source} reports, with {hf} and {hf2} leading the assault. Defenders say the invaders arrived without warning, without invitation and, worst of all, without bringing anything for the table.
According to {source}, the forces of {entity} fell upon {site} {ago} under the command of {hf}. Our military analyst rates the attack as 'loud' and the defence as 'also loud.'

War has come to {site}: {entity} launched an attack led by {hf}, says {source}. The fortress has been advised to check its drawbridge, its traps, and whether anyone remembered to train the militia this year.
Word from {source} is that {entity} struck {site} with a full army. Commanders {hf} and {hf2} reportedly disagreed on the plan, then attacked anyway, which historians call 'the usual approach.'
An invasion of {site} by {entity} is under way, reports {source}. Witnesses describe the scene as chaos, shouting and spears, which locals insist is 'quite different from a normal market day.'
The {entity_race} armies of {entity} have attacked {site}, according to {source}. {hf} is credited with leading the charge, and also with leading the subsequent argument over who gets the loot.

heads.text: ARMY CAMPS OUTSIDE, REFUSES TO LEAVE
TROOPS STARE AT WALLS FOR WEEKS

bodies.text: An army of {entity} led by {hf} is harassing {site}, {source} reports. The soldiers have reportedly been seen trampling crops, rattling gates and shouting rude things about local beards.
According to {source}, {hf} and the {entity_race} troops of {entity} have spent {season} pestering {site}. Residents describe the campaign as 'less a siege and more a very long, very rude visit.'

{site} remains under harassment by {entity}, says {source}. The army has neither attacked nor left, preferring to stand nearby looking menacing, a tactic our militia captain admits is 'honestly quite effective.'
Word via {source} is that forces under {hf} are harassing {site}. Locals say the soldiers mostly steal chickens and knock on doors at night, which the mayor has called 'a war crime against sleep.'

The {entity_race} army of {entity} continues to harass {site}, reports {source}. Commander {hf} is said to be waiting for the defenders to give up, while the defenders wait for the army to get bored. Bets are open.

Harassment of {site} by {entity} continues, according to {source}. Soldiers led by {hf} have reportedly broken fences, insulted goats and carved their names into the town well, which locals find 'deeply petty.'

heads.text: SOMEONE TAKEN IN THE NIGHT, AGAIN
MISSING: ONE PERSON, LAST SEEN BEING CARRIED
NIGHT RAID ENDS WITH ONE FEWER RESIDENT
KIDNAPPER STRIKES; DOORS FOUND TO LACK LOCKS
LOCAL TAKEN; FAMILY ASKS FOR HELP, ALE

bodies.text: {hf} has been abducted from {site} by {hf2}, {source} reports. The snatching took place {ago}, under cover of darkness, which our crime correspondent notes is 'the only kind of cover these people ever use.'
According to {source}, {hf2} crept into {site} and carried off {hf}. Locals have responded by installing new doors, new locks and a very large dog with no sense of humour.
Word reaches {fort} via {source} that {hf} was taken from {site} by {hf2}. The militia has been reminded to keep an eye on the children and, for that matter, the dwarves who act like children.
Abduction at {site}: {hf2} has made off with {hf}, says {source}. The {hf2_race} kidnapper reportedly left no ransom note, which experts consider rude even by kidnapping standards.
Grim news from {source}: {hf} was snatched from {site} {ago}. Suspicion has fallen on {hf2}, mainly because {hf2} was seen running off while carrying {hf}, which investigators call 'a strong lead.'
A {hf2_race} named {hf2} has abducted {hf} from {site}, {source} tells us. The town has requested better walls, more guards and, from the guards, fewer naps.
Report from {source}: {hf} has gone missing from {site}, taken by {hf2}. The fortress has once again checked that its gates close at night, and once again found a cat asleep in the mechanism.
{hf} was carried off from {site} by {hf2}, {source} reports. Neighbours describe the victim as 'a decent sort' and the kidnapper as 'definitely not a decent sort, look at those teeth.'
According to {source}, the kidnapper {hf2} struck at {site} {ago}, abducting {hf}. Officials urge everyone to report suspicious figures, which on a goblin border means 'basically everyone.'

The word from {source} is that {hf} has been abducted from {site}. The abductor, {hf2}, is believed to have fled toward the nearest dark fortress, which is the direction abductors always flee, oddly enough.

heads.text: HUGE THING SPOTTED, LOCALS SPOT EXITS
CREATURE IN THE HILLS, AND IT'S HUNGRY
FRONTIER TERROR STILL VERY MUCH ALIVE
BIG, SCALY, NOT HERE TO TRADE
DANGER LURKS; LIAISON LURKS FURTHER AWAY

bodies.text: The {hf_race} {hf} has been sighted at {site}, {source} reports. Residents are advised to stay indoors, avoid eye contact, and under no circumstances try to sell it anything at a discount.
According to {source}, the dreaded {hf} is roaming {region}. The beast, a {hf_race}, is said to be large, hungry and completely uninterested in the trade agreements we have so carefully drafted.
A warning from {source}: {hf}, a fearsome {hf_race}, has been seen near {site}. Our hunters volunteered to investigate, then immediately un-volunteered on learning what a {hf_race} is.

Beast sighting: {hf} the {hf_race} is reported in {region}, says {source}. Travellers are advised to take another road, or failing that, a slower friend. The {hf_race} is not believed to be fussy about which.

{hf} was seen lurking at {site} {ago}, {source} tells us. Witnesses describe the {hf_race} as 'enormous,' 'terrifying' and 'surprisingly good at doors.' Local carpenters are said to be both terrified and professionally impressed.
Word from {source}: the {hf_race} called {hf} has taken up residence near {site}. Property values have fallen sharply, while sales of sturdy boots and running lessons have soared.
A {hf_race} named {hf} prowls {region}, according to {source}. The militia commander has requested more crossbows, more bolts and, after some thought, a much larger fortress.
The beast {hf} is at {site}, reports {source}. Scholars at {fort} have already begun the engraving that will commemorate whatever happens next, leaving a blank space for the ending.

The monster {hf} has been reported in {region}, says {source}. Its diet is unknown, but locals note the {hf_race} has eaten three goats, a cart and one tax collector, which some consider a public service.

{hf}, a {hf_race} of dreadful reputation, is reported at {site}, {source} tells the fortress. Dwarves are reminded this is a perfect time to stay underground, which, conveniently, is where they already are.

heads.text: STRANGERS IN TOWN, AND LOTS OF THEM
CROWD REPORTED AT {site}, NOT FOR A PARTY
WHO ARE THEY? WHY ARE THEY THERE?
GROUP SIGHTED; GOSSIP MILL SIGHTED TOO

bodies.text: {entity}, a {entity_race} group, is present at {site}, {source} reports. What they want there is unclear; what they are doing there, witnesses say, is mostly standing about looking important.
According to {source}, members of {entity} have been seen at {site}. Our analysts are divided on whether this is a threat, a trade opportunity, or simply a very large picnic.

Word from {source} confirms the presence of {entity} at {site}. Local {entity_race} officials insist the group is 'just visiting,' a phrase historians note has preceded many of the region's less pleasant chapters.
The {entity_race} band known as {entity} has turned up at {site}, says {source}. The group has made no demands so far, though it has reportedly eaten everything in the tavern.
Reports reaching {fort} via {source} place {entity} at {site} {ago}. The bookkeeper has noted this in the ledger under 'things to worry about later,' which now runs to three volumes.
{entity} is at {site}, {source} tells us. Nobody at the depot could say why, but several merchants volunteered theories, most involving treasure and at least one involving an elaborate prank.
Word from {source}: a sizeable {entity_race} presence belonging to {entity} has settled in at {site}. Neighbours report noise, crowding and an alarming shortage of space for carts.
Per {source}, {entity} has a presence at {site}. The manager asks readers to remain calm, and also to remember which way the drawbridge lever goes, just in case.
The {entity_race} folk of {entity} are at {site}, according to {source}. Their purpose remains unknown, but one merchant swears he saw them buying a very large map and a very small apology card.
{entity} has gathered at {site}, notes {source}. The arrival was described by one witness as 'quiet, organised and frankly unsettling, like a goblin with a filing system.'

heads.text: GONE: ONE GROUP, NO FORWARDING ADDRESS
THEY LEFT. NOBODY KNOWS WHY. NOBODY ASKED

bodies.text: {entity} has left {site}, {source} reports. The group departed without ceremony, without explanation and, according to the innkeeper, without settling its tab, which the innkeeper has now framed and hung above the bar.
According to {source}, the {entity_race} group {entity} pulled out of {site} {ago}. Residents describe the mood as 'relieved,' 'curious' and 'slightly offended they didn't say goodbye.'
Word from {source} is that {entity} is no longer at {site}. Where they have gone is unknown, though our worriers have already worried that it might be here.
Departure news: {entity} has left {site}, says {source}. Locals report the only things left behind were a pile of empty barrels and a strong smell of {entity_race} cooking.
{entity} has moved on from {site}, according to {source}. Their departure leaves the town quieter, emptier and, the mayor admits, with far fewer people to blame for things.
Word via {source}: {entity} has left {site}. Analysts call it a strategic withdrawal; the group's own spokesman reportedly called it 'we got bored,' which analysts are choosing to ignore.

heads.text: LAST ONE OUT FORGETS TO LOCK UP
ABANDONED SITE SEEKS NEW TENANTS, ANY

bodies.text: {entity} has abandoned {site}, {source} reports. The once-busy {site_kind} now stands empty, home only to wind, dust and, inevitably, a few ambitious kobolds who have already started arguing over the best rooms.
According to {source}, {site} was abandoned by {entity} {ago}. Nobody is sure why, though theories include plague, monsters, bad water and 'they just fancied a change.'
Word via {source} is that {site} is deserted. Its former owners, {entity}, have simply left, which our property correspondent calls 'a bold way to end a lease.'
The {entity_race} group {entity} has walked away from {site}, says {source}. Scavengers are expected within the week, along with the usual squabble over who saw it first.
{site} is empty: {entity} has abandoned the {site_kind}, reports {source}. The fortress has been asked not to get ideas, which the expedition leader describes as 'too late.'
Word reaches {fort} via {source} that {entity} has given up on {site}. Departing residents reportedly left behind tables, beds and one very confused goat, who now runs the place.

heads.text: NEW TOWN ON THE MAP, AND IT'S SMUG
SETTLERS BREAK GROUND, AND SOME TOES
FOUNDING CEREMONY FEATURES ONE SPEECH TOO MANY

bodies.text: {entity} has founded {site}, a new {site_kind}, under the leadership of {hf}, {source} reports. The settlers are said to be proud, optimistic and wholly unaware of what lives in the nearest cave.
According to {source}, the {entity_race} folk of {entity} founded {site} {ago}. The founders have already built a wall, a well, and a tavern, in roughly the reverse of that order.
Word from {source} is that {hf} has led {entity} in founding {site}. The newcomers are reportedly asking around for advice; our manager suggests 'dig down, and do not dig too far.'
A new {site_kind} called {site} has been founded by {entity}, says {source}. Early reports describe the place as 'promising,' which in frontier terms means 'not yet on fire.'
{entity} has a new home: {site}, founded {ago}, reports {source}. Leader {hf} gave a speech at the founding, then a second speech, then was gently led away from the podium.
Founding news from {source}: {site} has been established by {entity}. Our expedition leader congratulates them warmly and reminds them that the first year is the easy part, and also the hard part.

heads.text: SETTLERS ON THE WAY, WAGONS CREAKING
PICKS OUT, PLANS DRAWN, ALE PACKED
SOMEONE IS STARTING A TOWN; WISH THEM LUCK

bodies.text: {entity} is founding a new settlement at {site}, led by {hf}, {source} reports. Settlers are said to be busy hauling timber, digging foundations and arguing about where the tavern should go.
According to {source}, the {entity_race} folk of {entity} are establishing {site}. Veterans of {fort} send their best wishes and one piece of advice: build the walls before the bedrooms.
Word via {source} is that work has begun on {site}, a {site_kind} being founded by {entity}. Early progress includes one hut, one fence and one long meeting about the second hut.
{hf} is leading {entity} in founding {site}, says {source}. The would-be settlers have reportedly already named the streets, the square and the tavern, but have not yet found any water.
Construction is under way at {site}, where {entity} is founding a new home, reports {source}. Neighbouring settlements have responded with a mixture of warm welcome and quietly planning raids.
Word via {source}: {entity} is setting up at {site}. Our engravers are already preparing a commemorative slab, leaving space for either 'and it prospered' or 'and then the carp came.'

heads.text: RECLAIMERS FIND HOME, SPIDERS, MORE SPIDERS
OLD HALLS FULL AGAIN, ECHOES CONFUSED
BACK AT LAST, AND THE ALE IS GONE

bodies.text: {entity} has reclaimed {site}, {source} reports. The returning {entity_race} settlers found the old halls dusty but intact, apart from the parts that were on fire, which have since stopped.
According to {source}, {site} is back in the hands of {entity} following a reclamation {ago}. Returnees say the place is just as they left it, if you ignore the bones, cobwebs and new monster nest.
Word from {source} is that {entity} has successfully reclaimed {site}. The settlers' first act was to search the cellars for any surviving ale; reports on the search are not encouraging.
Reclamation complete: {entity} holds {site} once more, says {source}. Historians note this is the sort of thing dwarves get very emotional about, and engravers get very busy about.
{site} has been reclaimed by {entity}, according to {source}. The settlers have started cleaning, repairing and complaining about whoever left the last mess, who was, technically, also them.
Word via {source}: {entity} has returned to {site} and taken it back. A ceremony was held in the old great hall, briefly interrupted when a forgotten trap went off under the mayor.

heads.text: THEY'RE GOING BACK. OF COURSE THEY ARE
OLD HOME, NEW ATTEMPT, SAME MONSTERS?
EXPEDITION SETS OUT TO TAKE BACK {site}
BRAVE OR FOOLISH: VOTE AT THE DEPOT

bodies.text: {entity} is attempting to reclaim {site}, {source} reports. The expedition is said to be well armed, well provisioned and only moderately nervous about whatever made them leave the first time.
According to {source}, the {entity_race} folk of {entity} are working to take back {site}. Our resident veteran wishes them luck and suggests checking the ceilings before celebrating.

Word via {source} is that a reclamation of {site} is under way by {entity}. Participants report progress, setbacks, and one unexpectedly hostile cupboard, which has since been defeated and turned into firewood.
{entity} has set out to reclaim {site}, says {source}. Old maps are being dusted off, old keys are being found, and old grudges against whatever lives there now are being sharpened.
Reclamation news via {source}: {entity} is retaking {site}, room by room. Early reports say the first three rooms went well; the fourth is 'being discussed.'
{site} may soon be inhabited again: {entity} is reclaiming it, {source} reports. Bookmakers at {fort} are offering generous odds, though nobody can agree on what the odds are for.

heads.text: TOWN RISES UP; OVERLORDS LIE DOWN?

bodies.text: An insurrection has broken out at {site} against {entity}, {source} reports. Rebels have taken to the streets with tools, torches and an extensive list of complaints, some of them about the bread.
According to {source}, the people of {site} have risen up against their {entity_race} rulers, {entity}. Officials describe the uprising as 'small'; the rebels describe it as 'just getting started.'
Word of revolt from {source}: {site} is in open insurrection against {entity}. Our political correspondent notes that occupations tend to end this way, usually with a lot of shouting first.
Uprising at {site}: locals are rebelling against {entity}, says {source}. Witnesses report barricades, banners and one surprisingly eloquent blacksmith who keeps standing on things to give speeches.
{site} has erupted in rebellion against {entity}, reports {source}. The rebels' demands reportedly include freedom, dignity and the immediate return of a confiscated cheese wheel.
Word reaches {fort} via {source} of an insurrection at {site}. {entity} is said to be furious; the rebels are said to be delighted; the town's barrel-maker is said to be rich.
The insurrection at {site} against {entity} has ended, {source} reports. Whether the rebels won, lost or simply went home for supper remains unclear, but the barricades are coming down.
According to {source}, the uprising in {site} is over. {entity} has declared order restored; the townsfolk have declared they 'will remember this,' which is what townsfolk always declare.
Word from {source} is that the revolt at {site} has come to an end. Furniture used in the barricades is being returned to its owners, mostly in more pieces than before.
Peace, of a sort, has returned to {site} following the end of the insurrection against {entity}, says {source}. Local historians are already arguing about what to call it.
The rebellion at {site} is finished, reports {source}. {entity} and the townspeople are reportedly back to their traditional relationship of mutual suspicion and grudging taxes.
Word via {source}: the uprising at {site} has ended. One rebel leader described the outcome as 'complicated,' then asked whether anyone at the depot was hiring.

heads.text: NEW RULER, SAME CROWN, SLIGHTLY BIGGER
OUT WITH THE OLD, IN WITH THE OLDER?
NEW LEADER VOWS CHANGE, ALSO MORE TAXES
LONG LIVE WHOEVER IT IS NOW
FRESH FACE TAKES THE BIG CHAIR

bodies.text: {hf} has succeeded {hf2} in a position of {entity}, {source} reports. The new office-holder has promised continuity, change and a fresh set of mandates, in that order.
According to {source}, {hf2} has been replaced by {hf} in the ranks of {entity}. Courtiers are busily removing old portraits and practising the new name, which several are still getting wrong.
Word from {source} is that {hf} now holds the office once held by {hf2}. Our bookkeeper warns that new nobles mean new demands, and has already ordered extra rock crystal, just in case.
Succession news: {hf} has taken over from {hf2} among {entity}, says {source}. Insiders describe the transition as smooth, except for a brief disagreement about who gets to keep the hat.
{entity} has a new face in charge: {hf}, successor to {hf2}, according to {source}. The new leader's first act was reportedly to sit in the chair; the second was to ask why it squeaks.
Word from {source}: {hf2} is out and {hf} is in at {entity}. Analysts expect business as usual, by which they mean feasts, grudges and at least one baffling decree about socks.
{hf} succeeded {hf2} {ago} in a post of {entity}, reports {source}. The fortress nobility have sent congratulations, along with a list of things they would also like to be put in charge of.
A change at the top: {source} reports {hf} has stepped into the role vacated by {hf2} within {entity}. The new title-holder is described as 'ambitious,' which in noble circles is not a compliment.
According to {source}, the {entity_race} realm of {entity} has seen {hf} succeed {hf2}. Engravers across the land have sighed heavily and started recarving the names on their monuments.
Confirmed by {source}: {hf} now holds the office of {hf2} within {entity}. Celebrations are planned, along with a review of all previous mandates, which is the part nobody is celebrating.
{hf} has claimed {site} for {entity}, {source} reports. The claim was made by pointing at the town and announcing it firmly, which our legal correspondent confirms is how most claims work.
According to {source}, {entity} now asserts ownership of {site}, thanks to a claim by {hf}. The residents of {site} were not consulted and are said to have 'thoughts.'
Word via {source} is that {hf} has staked a claim to {site} on behalf of {entity}. Neighbouring powers have responded with formal protests, informal shouting and a great deal of map-redrawing.
Claim news: {site} has been declared the property of {entity} by {hf}, says {source}. Experts call it either a bold political move or a misunderstanding about whose name was on the sign.
{hf} of {entity} has claimed {site}, according to {source}. Asked on what grounds, {hf} reportedly gestured at the ground, which observers admit is technically an answer.
Word via {source}: {hf} has formally claimed {site} for {entity}. The cartographer of {fort} has sighed, sharpened a quill and added yet another dotted line to the regional map.
{entity} has accepted an offer of tribute from {entity2}, {source} reports. Envoys {hf} and {hf2} sealed the deal over a long dinner, the cost of which was, inevitably, added to the tribute.
According to {source}, {entity2} offered tribute to {entity}, and {entity} said yes. Diplomats call it a triumph of negotiation; cynics call it a very polite protection racket.
Word from {source} is that a tribute arrangement between {entity} and {entity2} has been accepted. The first payment is due shortly, and the counting room has been dusted for the occasion.
Diplomatic news: {entity} agreed to accept tribute from {entity2}, says {source}. The envoy {hf} reportedly accepted the offer before it was finished being offered, to the dismay of everyone else.
{entity2} will now send tribute to {entity}, {source} reports, after the offer was formally accepted. Both sides describe the deal as 'fair,' a word that has never once been accurate in diplomacy.
Word via {source}: tribute offered by {entity2} has been accepted by {entity}. Merchants expect busier roads, heavier carts and, for a while at least, fewer burning villages.

heads.text: {entity} SAYS NO THANKS TO FREE STUFF
OFFER SPURNED, PRIDE INTACT, PURSE EMPTY

bodies.text: {entity} has refused an offer of tribute from {entity2}, {source} reports. Observers are puzzled, since refusing free goods is considered unusual everywhere, and outright suspicious among dwarves.
According to {source}, envoy {hf} turned down tribute offered by {entity2}. Diplomats suggest the refusal is a matter of pride; accountants suggest it is a matter of someone needing a lie-down.
Word from {source} is that the tribute offer of {entity2} has been rejected by {entity}. Analysts warn that people who refuse gifts usually prefer to take things the other way, with spears.
Tribute refused: {entity} declined the offer from {entity2}, says {source}. The rejected envoy, {hf2}, reportedly carried the gifts all the way home again, which sources call 'a long, quiet walk.'
{entity} will not accept tribute from {entity2}, {source} reports. A spokesperson explained that {entity} 'does not want gifts,' then paused meaningfully, which everyone found unsettling.
Word via {source}: an offer of tribute from {entity2} to {entity} has been flatly refused. Our bookkeeper has asked, with some feeling, whether that tribute is available to anyone else.

heads.text: PAY OR ELSE? THEY CHOSE PAY
'HAND IT OVER,' SAYS ENVOY. THEY DO

bodies.text: {entity2} has accepted a demand for tribute from {entity}, {source} reports. Payments will begin shortly, and the treasury of {entity2} has reportedly begun weeping quietly in a corner.
According to {source}, {entity} demanded tribute from {entity2} and got it. Envoy {hf} described the talks as 'productive'; the other side described them as 'having a sword pointed at us.'
Word from {source} is that {entity2} will pay tribute to {entity} after accepting its demands. Historians note this is the diplomatic equivalent of handing over your lunch money, but with banners.
Tribute demand accepted: {entity2} has agreed to the terms of {entity}, says {source}. The decision was said to be unanimous, if you count only the people who were not glaring at the envoy.
{entity} demanded, {entity2} accepted, {source} reports. Carts of goods will soon travel between the two, accompanied by armed guards, sour faces and an exhaustive inventory.
Word via {source}: the envoy {hf2} of {entity2} has agreed to pay tribute to {entity}. Our bookkeeper notes this with interest, and with fervent hope that nobody gets the same idea about us.

heads.text: ENVOY SENT HOME WITH EMPTY CART
NO TRIBUTE, SAYS PROUD REALM; WAR NEXT?

bodies.text: {entity2} has refused a demand for tribute from {entity}, {source} reports. The envoy who made the demand was sent home empty-handed, apart from a firm reply and a rather pointed turnip.

According to {source}, {entity} demanded tribute and {entity2} said no. Military analysts are already sharpening their predictions, and the militias on both sides are sharpening absolutely everything else they own.
Word from {source} is that {entity2} rejected the tribute demands of {entity}. Envoy {hf} reportedly delivered the refusal in person, then left the room very quickly, as is customary.

Tribute refused: {entity2} will not pay {entity}, says {source}. A spokesperson described the demand as 'insulting,' 'unreasonable' and 'written on very cheap paper,' then tore it up, which took longer than expected.
The tribute demand of {entity} has been flatly rejected by {entity2}, according to {source}. Observers expect either renewed negotiations or a short war, and are quietly betting on the second.
Word via {source}: {entity2} has told {entity} exactly where it can put its tribute demand. Our diplomatic correspondent declined to repeat the location, citing family readership.

heads.text: ENVOYS SIGN PEACE, KEEP DAGGERS NEARBY
TREATY SIGNED; ARMIES HOME FOR SUPPER

bodies.text: {entity} has accepted a peace offer from {entity2}, {source} reports. Envoys {hf} and {hf2} signed the agreement, shook hands, and immediately counted their fingers, as is diplomatic custom.
According to {source}, the fighting between {entity} and {entity2} is officially over. Both sides claim victory, both sides blame the other for starting it, and both sides are very tired.
Word from {source} is that the peace offer of {entity2} has been accepted by {entity}. Soldiers on both sides have been sent home, where several reportedly found their families had redecorated.
Peace news: {entity} and {entity2} have agreed to stop fighting, says {source}. Weaponsmiths report a sudden slump in orders, while tavern keepers report a sudden boom.
{entity} said yes to peace with {entity2}, according to {source}. The treaty is said to be twelve pages long, eleven of which are about who started it.
Word via {source}: {entity} and {entity2} are at peace following an accepted offer. Our militia commander welcomed the news, then asked for the war budget anyway, 'just in case.'

heads.text: WAR CONTINUES; TREATY USED AS KINDLING

bodies.text: {entity} has refused an offer of peace from {entity2}, {source} reports. The war will therefore continue, to the great disappointment of everyone except the armourers.
According to {source}, peace talks between {entity} and {entity2} have collapsed. Envoy {hf} reportedly rejected the proposal before it was fully read, citing 'a bad feeling about page two.'
Word from {source} is that the peace offer of {entity2} was turned down by {entity}. Military analysts expect the fighting to continue, and frankly so does everyone who has met either side.
Peace refused: {entity} will keep fighting {entity2}, says {source}. The rejected treaty was returned with a note reading 'no,' which diplomats concede was at least admirably clear.
{entity} has rejected peace with {entity2}, {source} reports. The envoy {hf2} is said to have taken the news calmly, then walked outside and kicked a fence for some time.
Word via {source}: there will be no peace between {entity} and {entity2}, at least not this season. Caravans travelling between them are advised to bring extra guards and a white flag, both.

heads.text: NO MORE FREE STUFF, SAYS FORMER PAYER
TRIBUTE ENDED; CART SOLD FOR SCRAP
DEAL OFF: THE GRAVY WAGON HAS LEFT

bodies.text: Tribute between {entity} and {entity2} is to cease, {source} reports. The arrangement, long a source of quiet resentment on one side and quiet delight on the other, is now just quiet.
According to {source}, {entity} has offered to end the tribute arrangement with {entity2}. One treasury is said to be celebrating, while the other is said to be checking under the cushions.

Word from {source} is that tribute payments between {entity} and {entity2} are coming to an end. Experts warn that ending tribute is like ending a lease: someone is always surprised and someone is always cross.
No more tribute: {entity} and {entity2} have agreed to call it off, says {source}. Envoys {hf} and {hf2} reportedly marked the occasion with a toast, a handshake and a long, suspicious look.
The tribute flowing between {entity2} and {entity} will stop, according to {source}. Carters who hauled the payments are seeking new work and have asked if {fort} needs anything heavy moved.
Word via {source}: an end has been offered to the tribute deal between {entity} and {entity2}. Analysts call it a sign of improved relations, worsened relations, or both, depending on who pays them.

heads.text: FAMED TREASURE TURNS UP, AS THEY DO
LEGENDARY ITEM FOUND, NOT IN A SOCK
WHERE IS THE ARTIFACT? THERE, APPARENTLY
PRIZED RELIC SPOTTED; GREED SPOTTED TOO
THAT FAMOUS THING IS IN THAT PLACE

bodies.text: The artifact {artifact}, a {artifact_item}, is held at {site}, {source} reports. Collectors are said to be very excited; the people who run the {site_kind} are said to be buying more locks.

According to {source}, {artifact} can be found at {site}. The {artifact_item} is described as 'priceless,' 'legendary' and 'not for sale, so please stop asking.' Several merchants at our depot have asked anyway, twice.
Word from {source} is that the famed {artifact_item} {artifact} rests at {site}. Our craftsdwarves have responded by staring moodily at their workshops and muttering about inspiration.
Artifact news: {artifact} is at {site}, says {source}. The {artifact_item} has reportedly been the subject of three theft attempts, two duels and one very long poem.
{artifact}, the celebrated {artifact_item}, is reported at {site} by {source}. Historians note it has changed hands many times, usually by force and usually at night.
Word via {source}: {artifact} is kept at {site}. Locals say the {artifact_item} is guarded day and night, though the night guard is reportedly 'mostly asleep.'
Confirmed by {source}: the legendary {artifact} is at {site}. The mayor of {fort} asked whether it might be borrowed for a feast; the answer, delivered by a caravan guard, was a laugh.
The {artifact_item} known as {artifact} is at {site}, according to {source}. A merchant who claims to have seen it calls it 'shiny, beautiful and much heavier than you'd think when running.'
Reports place {artifact} at {site}, {source} tells us. The {artifact_item} is said to be well looked after, polished weekly, and spoken to kindly by at least one caretaker.
According to {source}, {site} is home to {artifact}, a {artifact_item} of great renown. Several adventurers have set off to see it, several more to steal it, and one simply wants to touch it.

heads.text: LEGENDARY ITEM IN THE WILDS, UNSUPERVISED
MASTERWORK LYING IN THE MUD, REPORTEDLY

bodies.text: {artifact}, a {artifact_item}, is somewhere in {region}, {source} reports. The relic is believed to be lying in the open, unguarded and, crucially, not yet picked up by an elf.
According to {source}, the famed {artifact} has been lost in {region}. Treasure hunters are advised to bring a map, a shovel and a strong sense of what a {artifact_item} looks like.
Word from {source} is that {artifact} lies somewhere in the wilds of {region}. Merchants report a sudden surge in sales of lanterns, shovels and nervous expeditions.
Lost artifact: {artifact} is reported in {region}, says {source}. The {artifact_item} is presumed to be getting rained on, which our craftsdwarves describe as 'an absolute tragedy.'
{artifact} is out there in {region}, according to {source}. Several parties are said to be searching for the {artifact_item}, and several more are said to be following them.
Word via {source}: a legendary {artifact_item}, {artifact}, lies somewhere in {region}. Our expedition leader asks that nobody go looking for it during working hours, again.

heads.text: WHO HAS THE RELIC? WE HAVE A NAME
OWNER OF FAMOUS ITEM REFUSES TO SHARE

bodies.text: {artifact}, a {artifact_item}, is in the possession of {hf}, {source} reports. The holder is said to carry it everywhere, including to dinner, to bed and, by some accounts, to the bath.

According to {source}, {hf} has {artifact}. The {artifact_item} is described as priceless, and {hf} is described as 'unbearable about it.' Dinner guests report hearing the full story of its making, at length, every evening.
Word from {source} is that the famed {artifact} is held by {hf}. Many have asked to see the {artifact_item}; few have been allowed; one was allowed and has not stopped talking about it.
Artifact whereabouts: {hf} carries {artifact}, says {source}. Thieves across the region are said to be updating their lists, and {hf} is said to be updating the guards.
{hf} is the current holder of {artifact}, according to {source}. Asked how the {artifact_item} was acquired, {hf} reportedly smiled and changed the subject to the weather.
Word via {source}: {artifact} travels with {hf}, a {hf_race}. Our craftsdwarves ask whether {hf} might visit {fort} sometime, purely to admire it, and absolutely not for any other reason.

heads.text: WHERE DID IT GO? NOBODY KNOWS
FAMOUS TREASURE NOT WHERE IT SHOULD BE
HEIST SUSPECTED, OR VERY BAD FILING

bodies.text: {artifact}, a {artifact_item}, is no longer at {site}, {source} reports. The empty spot where it once sat has become a popular attraction in its own right, drawing crowds of confused visitors.
According to {source}, the famed {artifact} has gone missing from {site}. Investigators suspect theft, misplacement, or 'one of those adventurer types,' which locals agree is the same thing.
Word from {source} is that {artifact} is not at {site}, where it was last known to be. Its keepers insist they 'only looked away for a moment,' a moment some estimate at several years.

Missing artifact: {artifact} has vanished from {site}, says {source}. A reward is offered for the return of the {artifact_item}, no questions asked, though several questions are clearly being thought.
{artifact} is gone from {site}, according to {source}. The town launched a search, checked under every bed and found three lost socks, a cat and no {artifact_item}.
Word via {source}: {site} no longer has {artifact}. Our bookkeeper has quietly checked that every artifact in {fort} is where it belongs, and found one being used as a doorstop.

heads.text: IT WAS PERFECT. IT WAS. PAST TENSE

bodies.text: {artifact}, a {artifact_item} of great renown, has been destroyed, {source} reports. The craftsdwarves of {fort} have declared a day of mourning, which they are spending loudly in the tavern.
According to {source}, the famed {artifact} is no more. How the {artifact_item} was destroyed is unclear, but witnesses agree it involved 'a lot of noise and then a sad little clink.'
Word from {source} is that {artifact} has been destroyed. Historians are grief-stricken, collectors are devastated, and one elderly engraver has simply put down his chisel and stared at the wall.
Tragedy: the {artifact_item} {artifact} was destroyed {ago}, says {source}. Our own legendary crafter took the news badly and has been in a strange mood ever since, which could go either way.
{artifact} has been lost forever, {source} reports, destroyed in circumstances nobody is keen to discuss. The remains, if any, are reportedly kept in a small box labelled 'do not.'
Word via {source}: {artifact} is destroyed. The {artifact_item} was said to be one of the finest ever made, and is now one of the finest ever unmade, which is far less impressive.

flee.text: Refugees of {entity2} fled {site} ahead of the army of {entity}; the ale reportedly did not make it.
{site} has been emptied as the {entity_race} forces of {hf} approach, says {source}.
Residents fled {site} {ago}, citing 'an army' and 'a really bad feeling.'
{entity} marched on {site} and found it politely vacated.

occupation.text: {entity} has occupied {site}, evicting {entity2} and most of the furniture.
{site} has been under {entity_race} occupation since {ago}, says {source}.
{entity2} was evicted from {site}; forwarding address: 'the woods, presumably.'
The {entity_race} occupiers of {site} report the place 'smaller than it looked on the map.'

invasion.text: {entity} attacked {site}, led by {hf}; the gate is reported to have opinions about it.
Fighting broke out at {site} {ago} as {entity} invaded, says {source}.
{hf} and {hf2} led an assault on {site} and are already taking credit.
{site} is under attack by {entity}; the outpost liaison asks us not to panic loudly.

harass.text: The army of {hf} is harassing {site}, mostly by being rude near it.
{entity} continues to bother {site}; residents report 'a lot of loitering.'
Troops of {entity} are harassing {site}, says {source}; the goats are not coping.
The {entity_race} raiders at {site} have neither attacked nor gone home, which is somehow worse.

abduction.text: {hf2} abducted {hf} from {site} {ago}; doors across the region are being locked twice.
{hf} was snatched from {site}, says {source}; the kidnapper {hf2} left no note.
Abduction at {site}: {hf} taken, {hf2} blamed, guards embarrassed.
Another kidnapping near {site}; the {hf2_race} {hf2} is the prime suspect.

beast.text: The {hf_race} {hf} has been seen at {site}; please lock the gate and the good cheese.
{hf} is roaming {region}, says {source}; nobody is volunteering to check.
A {hf_race} called {hf} lurks near {site}, and it is not here for the caravan.
Beast warning for {region}: {hf} is out and about, and peckish.

group.text: {entity} has been seen at {site}, doing something; details to follow, possibly never.
A {entity_race} group, {entity}, is present at {site}, says {source}.
{entity} is at {site}; locals are counting their chickens, literally.
Merchants report {entity} gathered at {site} {ago}, looking busy.

leave.text: {entity} has left {site}; the tavern reports a large unpaid tab.
The {entity_race} folk of {entity} have gone from {site}, and locals are cautiously stretching out.
{site} has seen the back of {entity}, for now.

abandon.text: {entity} abandoned {site} {ago}; the kobolds have already moved in, probably.
{site} stands empty after {entity} gave up on it, says {source}.
The {site_kind} of {site} is abandoned; one goat remains, reportedly in charge.
{entity} has left {site} to the dust and the rumours.

founded.text: {entity} founded {site}, a new {site_kind}, {ago}; the tavern opened the same afternoon.
A new {entity_race} {site_kind}, {site}, now exists, and wants you to know it.
{site} was founded by {entity}; the welcome sign is already misspelled.

founding.text: {entity} is founding {site}; the first argument concerns the tavern's location.
Settlers led by {hf} are building {site}, says {source}.
{site} is under construction by {entity}, currently one hut and a dream.
The {entity_race} folk of {entity} are founding a {site_kind} at {site}; good luck to them.

reclaimed.text: {site} is home again to {entity}, says {source}, spiders and all.
The old {site_kind} of {site} has been retaken by {entity}.

reclaiming.text: {entity} is reclaiming {site}; the old locks reportedly still work, unfortunately.
An expedition from {entity} is retaking {site}, says {source}.
Reclamation of {site} is under way; the monsters inside have not been consulted.
{entity} wants {site} back and is going in to get it.

insurrection.text: {site} has risen up against {entity}; barricades made of furniture are reported.
Insurrection at {site}, says {source}; {entity} is not amused.
Rebels at {site} demand freedom from {entity}, and better bread.
The people of {site} have had enough of {entity}, and are saying so loudly.

insurrection_end.text: The uprising at {site} against {entity} is over; the sweeping has begun.
Calm returns to {site}; the rebels' banners are being reused as tablecloths.
{entity} reports the revolt at {site} finished; the rebels report otherwise, quietly.

succession.text: {hf} has succeeded {hf2} in {entity}; the hat reportedly fits.
{hf2} is out, {hf} is in; mandates are expected shortly.
{entity} has a new leader in {hf}, and engravers have a lot of recarving to do.

claim.text: {hf} claims {site} for {entity}; the townsfolk are still looking for the paperwork.
A claim on {site} has been made by {hf}, mostly by pointing.
{site} has been claimed for {entity}, and the map-makers are tired.

accept_tribute_offer.text: {entity} accepted tribute from {entity2}; the counting room is delighted.
A tribute offer between {entity2} and {entity} was accepted, says {source}.
Envoys {hf} and {hf2} agreed a tribute deal, then argued about the dinner bill.
{entity2} will pay tribute to {entity}, and both say they are thrilled.

refuse_tribute_offer.text: {entity} refused tribute from {entity2}; nobody understands why, least of all the bookkeepers.
A tribute offer was declined by {entity}, says {source}.
Envoy {hf} said no to free goods, a decision historians will study for years.
{entity2} offered tribute; {entity} said no; tension follows.

accept_tribute_demand.text: {entity2} agreed to pay tribute to {entity}; the treasury is in mourning.
The tribute demand of {entity} was accepted, says {source}.
Envoy {hf2} said yes to tribute, through gritted teeth.
{entity} asked for tribute and, alarmingly, got it.

refuse_tribute_demand.text: {entity2} refused to pay tribute to {entity}; the armouries report brisk business.
The tribute demands of {entity} were rejected, says {source}.
{entity2} said no to {entity}, and said it loudly.
No tribute will be paid to {entity}, and everyone is bracing.

accept_peace_offer.text: {entity} accepted peace with {entity2}; both sides claim to have won.
Peace has been agreed between {entity} and {entity2}, says {source}.
Envoys {hf} and {hf2} signed a peace treaty and, astonishingly, nobody stabbed anyone.
The war between {entity} and {entity2} is over, pending the next one.

refuse_peace_offer.text: {entity} rejected peace with {entity2}; the armourers are delighted.
Peace talks between {entity} and {entity2} failed, says {source}.
Envoy {hf} said no to peace, then asked what was for lunch.
No peace for {entity2}: {entity} would rather keep fighting.

cease_tribute_offer.text: Tribute between {entity} and {entity2} is to stop; one treasury cheers.
{entity} has offered to end tribute with {entity2}, says {source}.
The tribute carts between {entity} and {entity2} will roll no more.
The tribute deal between {entity} and {entity2} is over, and somebody's treasurer is smiling.

artifact_in_site.text: {artifact}, a {artifact_item}, is at {site}; please do not lick it.
{site} holds {artifact}, and its guards hold their breath.
Merchants report {artifact} kept at {site}, polished and much admired.

artifact_in_subregion.text: {artifact} lies somewhere in {region}; finders are advised to wipe it first.
Treasure alert: {artifact} is out in the wilds of {region}.
{artifact} is in {region}, unguarded, and now everyone knows it.

artifact_in_inventory.text: {hf} has {artifact} and will not stop mentioning it.
{artifact} is in the hands of {hf}; thieves have been informed, sadly.
{hf} keeps {artifact} close, reportedly even at bedtime.

artifact_not_in_site.text: {artifact} is missing from {site}; the plinth is taking it hard.
The {artifact_item} {artifact} is no longer at {site}, says {source}.
{site} has lost track of {artifact}; a reward is offered.
Nobody at {site} can find {artifact}, and everybody is blaming adventurers.

artifact_destroyed.text: {artifact} has been destroyed; craftsdwarves everywhere are taking the day off to grieve.
{artifact} was destroyed {ago}, and history is not pleased.
The legendary {artifact_item} {artifact} has been smashed, broken or otherwise ruined.

pouch.text: The Diplomatic Pouch is open, courtesy of {source}, and it is full of news nobody at {fort} was ready for.
Fresh rumours have arrived at {fort} by way of {source}; here is what the wider world has been up to.
News from beyond the walls, delivered by {source} and only lightly embellished by this paper.
The world outside {fort} has been busy, according to {source}; here are the highlights, lowlights and middle-lights.
Our correspondent cornered {source} at the trade depot and refused to let go until we had the news.
Diplomatic dispatches have reached {fort}; read them now, before the nobles find a way to tax them.
Word from the wider world, brought to {fort} by {source} and paid for with one mug of ale.
The pouch has arrived, slightly damp, courtesy of {source}; here is everything that was still legible.
Hot off the trade road: {source} brings the following reports from across the land.
This season's rumours, gathered from {source} and checked against absolutely nothing.
The outside world sends its regards and its troubles to {fort}; here are both.
Stop the forges: news has come in from {source}, and some of it may even be true.
Gathered at the depot, sorted in the tavern, printed here: the latest from {source}.
A satchel of foreign news has been emptied onto the depot floor at {fort}, and we picked up every scrap.

depot_gossip.text: One of the merchants swore that {entity} is up to something at {site}, then charged the bookkeeper three coins for the rest of the story.
Overheard at the depot: a caravan guard says {site} has the worst ale in the land, and he would know, because he drank all of it.
Word is that {source} told the broker {hf} is 'taller in person,' which nobody asked about but everyone remembered.
A trader at the depot claims the {entity_race} folk of {entity} have been eyeing the walls of {fort}. The mason has since been seen eyeing them too, nervously.
Talk at the depot is that {site} has run out of socks entirely. The clothier is already calculating export prices, and smiling.
One merchant insisted {hf} once traded a whole cart for a single wheel of cheese. Another merchant insisted it was a very good cheese.
The broker says {source} talks too much. The broker then talked for an hour about {source}, which several dwarves found ironic.
Gossip from the wagons: {entity} keeps a pet carp at {site}, named after an old enemy, and feeds it only during {season}.
A pack-animal handler claims {site} is haunted. The pack animal, consulted separately, declined to comment.
The caravan cook told our cook that {entity} serves elf food at feasts now. Our cook has not stopped shaking his head since.
At the depot, {source} hinted that {hf} owes money to half the region, and an apology to the other half.
A merchant said the {entity_race} folk at {site} have a law against beards. The whole fortress gasped, then went back to work.
Rumour at the trade depot: a kobold was elected to something at {site}. Nobody can confirm it, but everybody wants it to be true.
One of the caravan guards claims {hf} can lift an anvil with one hand. Another guard says it was a small anvil and a large hand.
Overheard by the stockpiles: the merchants say {fort} is famous now. They would not say what for, which is concerning.
Apparently {source} believes the roads near {site} are full of goblins, elves and tax collectors, 'in descending order of politeness.'
A trader swore an elf at {site} apologised to a tree for an hour. The dwarves listening found this both baffling and deeply on-brand.
Depot chatter: {entity} has been buying rope in vast quantities. Nobody knows why, everybody has a theory, and most theories involve a very large cliff.
A merchant claimed {hf} was once beaten at arm-wrestling by a goat. The goat was unavailable for comment, being busy pulling the wagon.
Word slipped from {source} that the capital considers {fort} 'a nice little hobby.' The fortress is taking this extremely personally.
Merchants claim {site} has more guards than residents. The guards reportedly guard each other now, out of habit and boredom.
One caravan driver insists {entity} once lost a war over a misread map. He then sold our bookkeeper a map, at full price.
The broker overheard {source} say that {hf} is planning something big. Asked what, {source} reportedly repeated 'something big,' but slower.
Gossip from the depot: the {entity_race} folk of {entity} think dwarves are 'a bit much.' The dwarves who overheard this agreed, proudly.
A teamster claims the wells of {site} taste of iron. Our miners have asked for directions and an extra-large bucket.
Word among the wagons is that {hf} sleeps in full armour, just in case. Our militia captain nodded approvingly and took notes.
One merchant whispered that {site} pays its taxes in turnips. The tax collector of {fort} has gone very quiet and very thoughtful.
The merchants say {entity} owes {entity2} an apology, a goat and a fence, in that order. Negotiations are reportedly stuck on the goat.
Supposedly {source} saw a necromancer buying candles in bulk near {site}. The candle-maker of {fort} has declared this 'good for business.'
Overheard at the trade depot: the caravan mule bit {source}. The broker recorded this in the ledger as 'a fair trade.'
Merchants report that {site} holds a festival every {season} at which nobody may mention goblins. Attendance, they say, is enormous.
A wagon guard says the roads from {site} are safe now. The other wagon guards laughed so hard that one of them fell off the wagon.
One trader claims {hf} has never once lost a game of dice. Another trader claims that is because {hf} owns all the dice.
Depot whispers suggest {entity} is running short of ale. Our brewer has offered to help, for a price, with a very wide grin.
Apparently {source} told the bookkeeper that {site} is 'lovely this time of year.' The bookkeeper checked: it is {season}, and the place is reportedly flooded.
A merchant swears the elves of {site} have outlawed axes. Our woodcutter has quietly cancelled any holiday plans in that direction.
Overheard: a caravan guard believes {hf} is secretly three kobolds in a long coat. Evidence is thin, but the coat is said to be very long.
The merchants claim {entity} sends envoys everywhere except {fort}. The manager says that is fine, absolutely fine, totally fine.
At the depot, {source} was overheard admitting the caravan almost turned back at the first carp. Nobody at {fort} blames them.
Merchant gossip says the nobles of {site} issue three mandates a day. Our own nobles have heard this and are reportedly 'inspired.'
A trader insists that {hf} once out-shouted a dragon. The dragon, presumably, has a different version of events.
Talk at the depot is that {entity} and {entity2} are not speaking. The merchants carry messages between them, and charge both sides double.
One of the teamsters says the goblins of {site} have started a book club. The first book is reportedly about stealing books.
According to {source}, a merchant's hat blew off near {site} and was later seen on the head of a goblin general, who wore it well.
